function: DDQN learns UAV 3D movement and per-user power allocation for downlink throughput; the RIS phase shift is set by a closed-form rule (Eq. 33), not learned (pp. 9-10).
system: Three single-antenna UAV base stations, six single-antenna UEs, downlink NOMA with imperfect SIC; passive reflecting RIS, 10x10 elements, on a building; 2 GHz carrier (pp. 2, 4, 11).
method: Double DQN (three fully connected layers, 40 hidden neurons) trained by reinforcement learning with experience replay, random initialization; K-means clusters users (pp. 9-11).
data_channel: Custom simulator: UAV-UE path loss and LoS probability follow 3GPP TR 36.777, fading is a random variable, RIS-UE links are LoS; no dataset or measurements (pp. 4-5, 16).
test_conditions: Trained and reported in one simulator as throughput per training episode; numbers of UAVs (1-4), users (6-12) and PRUs are varied, each with its own curve (pp. 13-14).
baselines: Non-learned: Random actions, fixed and random power allocation, OMA, no RIS, no phase optimization. Learned: DQN, Dueling-DQN, discrete actor-critic, DDQN with random clustering (pp. 12-13).
metrics: System throughput (Mbits), energy efficiency, user satisfaction index, average reward, execution and update time (pp. 12-14).
complexity: Overall O(UKN + ET(|S||A|LBU + M^2)); DNN O(|S|L + |A|L + L); execution time 30.45-51.74 ms, update time 114.84-169.72 ms (pp. 11, 14).
openness: none; no link to code or data (simulation setup on p. 11 names only Python, Scikit-learn and Tensorflow).
q1_support: p. 4: "is a random variable that represents the fading"; only the UAV-UE path loss and LoS probability (Eqs. 4-5) follow 3GPP TR 36.777 [39], fading is custom, RIS-UE links are plain LoS, and no TR 38.901, TR 38.811, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 14: "we investigate the performance of system throughputs under different numbers of UEs"; Figs. 7 and 11-13 plot throughput per training episode for each setting, so no trained model is tested in unseen conditions and no adaptation is reported.
q3_support: p. 12: "Some benchmarks are introduced, including the Random, DQN, DDQN," and Dueling-DQN and discrete actor-critic; the Random scheme draws movement, phase shift and power at random (non-learned), and the proposed scheme gains about 57% throughput over DQN.
q4_support: p. 11: "the overall computational complexity of the proposed algorithm is O(U KN + ET (|S||A|LBU + M 2 ))"; Table IV (p. 14) gives execution time of 30.45 to 51.74 ms.
q5_support: p. 11: "experiment is performed using Python 3.7, Scikit-learn 1.3.0 and" Tensorflow 1.15.0; no link, DOI or public dataset is given, and the channel is simulated.
notes: Area 6: the learned DDQN controls UAV movement (above the physical layer) jointly with per-user transmit power (physical layer in aerial links), so it passes above_phy (p. 9). The RIS phase shift is not learned: Algorithm 2 step 10 'Obtain optimal phase shift by (33)' (p. 9) is a closed-form alignment taken from [25] (p. 10), although the abstract presents it as jointly optimized. Area 3 therefore does not fit, and area 6 precedes it anyway. q1: only path loss and LoS probability come from 3GPP TR 36.777 (a UAV study, not TR 38.901 or 38.811), reviewer to confirm. q2: no unseen-condition test. q3: the benchmark DDQN differs from the proposed scheme only by random clustering instead of K-means, so it is an ablation and is not counted; DQN, Dueling-DQN and discrete actor-critic are the learned baselines. Table I (p. 3) compares features of earlier works, not performance.
